question: Which type of report in OneStream is described as a grid-based view of cube data?

options.A: Cube View
options.B: Report Book
options.C: Form
options.D: Dashboard

explanation: A is correct: a Cube View is the OneStream report type that presents cube data in a grid-based format, allowing users to query and display multidimensional data in rows and columns. B is incorrect — Report Books are containers that combine multiple reports into a single output. C is incorrect — Forms are used for data entry, not grid-based cube data viewing. D is incorrect — Dashboards are interactive screens that include multiple components.

question: What are two reasons executive reports are created in OneStream? (Select 2.)

options.A: To analyze executive productivity metrics.
options.B: To help executives identify their line manager.
options.C: To help executives make business-related decisions.
options.D: To provide executives with a high-level summary of company financial performance.

explanation: C and D are correct: executive reports are created to help executives make business-related decisions and to provide high-level financial summaries that executives can quickly consume. A is incorrect — analyzing executive productivity is an HR function, not a financial reporting purpose. B is incorrect — identifying line managers is an organizational concern, not a financial reporting use case.

question: What is the purpose of ad hoc analysis in OneStream?

options.A: To empower users to create report books.
options.B: To embed PDF reports into the Spreadsheet tool.
options.C: To empower users to create their own reports.
options.D: To generate reports outside of normal working hours.

explanation: C is correct: ad hoc analysis empowers users to create their own reports on demand using tools like Quick Views and Cube View Connections, without requiring pre-built reports from a developer. A is incorrect — report books are a separate report type, not the definition of ad hoc analysis. B is incorrect — embedding PDFs in Spreadsheet is a specific capability, not the definition of ad hoc analysis. D is incorrect — report scheduling is a separate feature unrelated to ad hoc analysis.

question: A customer wants to restrict a user to view only Actual data and only the OwnerPreAdj Consolidation member. Which two dimensions would be used to apply these specific requirements? (Select 2.)

options.A: Account
options.B: Time
options.C: Scenario
options.D: Consolidation

explanation: C and D are correct: to restrict a user to Actual data only, Scenario dimension security is applied; to restrict access to the OwnerPreAdj member only, Consolidation dimension security is applied. A is incorrect — Account security controls which accounts are accessible, not Scenario or Consolidation restrictions. B is incorrect — Time dimension security restricts which time periods a user can access, not the Scenario or Consolidation member.

question: Which type of table in OneStream is described as a staging area containing imported data and/or attributes?

options.A: BI Blend Tables
options.B: Stage Tables
options.C: Solution Tables
options.D: Cube Tables

explanation: B is correct: Stage Tables serve as the staging area that contains imported data and/or attributes — they hold data that has been loaded before it is processed into the cube. A is incorrect — BI Blend Tables are relational tables optimized for reporting on large data sets. C is incorrect — Solution Tables contain data used in MarketPlace solutions. D is incorrect — Cube Tables is not a standard OneStream classification in this context.

question: What is the purpose of a dynamic report in OneStream?

options.A: Displays static data that cannot be changed by the user.
options.B: Displays personalized data for the user based on their context.
options.C: Can be viewed on a tablet device only.
options.D: Allows a user to change the font of the report.

explanation: B is correct: a dynamic report displays personalized data for the user — it adapts based on the user's security profile, workflow context, or POV selections, showing each user the data relevant to their role. A is incorrect — static data describes a fixed report, not a dynamic one. C is incorrect — dynamic reports are not limited to tablet access. D is incorrect — font changes are a formatting feature, not the definition of a dynamic report.

question: Which two sliders are shown on the Designer tab when creating a Cube View in OneStream? (Select 2.)

options.A: POV
options.B: Common
options.C: Layout
options.D: Report Footer

explanation: A and D are correct: the POV slider and the Report Footer slider are shown on the Designer tab when creating a Cube View. B is incorrect — Common is not one of the Designer tab sliders. C is incorrect — Layout is not a Designer tab slider in the Cube View designer.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Profiles and Groups
question: What is the purpose of using a Cube View Profile in OneStream?

options.A: To control how Groups, and the Cube Views within them, are accessed.
options.B: To control the size of headers and footers in a Cube View.
options.C: To enable assigning a Cube View to a specific Entity.
options.D: To control how Forms and Dashboards are accessed.

explanation: A is correct: a Cube View Profile controls how Groups — and the Cube Views within those Groups — are accessed by users. B is incorrect — header and footer sizes are formatting settings within the Cube View itself. C is incorrect — assigning a Cube View to a specific Entity is done via POV settings. D is incorrect — Forms and Dashboards have their own access control mechanisms.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Profiles and Groups
question: Why are Cube View Groups added to Cube View Profiles?

options.A: It makes it easier to locate Cube Views within the application.
options.B: Profiles control how the Cube Views within the groups are accessed.
options.C: Profiles control how individual users are assigned to the Cube View.
options.D: It makes it easier to locate each member within the application.

explanation: B is correct: Cube View Groups are added to Profiles because Profiles control how the Cube Views within those Groups are accessed — determining which users or roles can see and use those Cube Views. A is incorrect — while Groups aid discoverability, the primary reason is access control, not navigation. C is incorrect — Profiles control group-level access, not individual user assignments. D is incorrect — member location is a metadata concern, not a Cube View Profile function.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: Which of the following is an example of a Member Expansion in a Cube View Member Filter?

options.B: E#LE_110.Base
options.D: E#Base

explanation: B is correct: E#LE_110.Base is a Member Expansion — the expansion keyword (Base) is appended after the member reference using a period, retrieving all base-level members under LE_110. A is incorrect — E#LE_110 is a single member filter without any expansion. C is incorrect — a comma-separated list is not a Member Expansion. D is incorrect — E#Base alone is not standard Member Expansion syntax.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: Which of the following is an example of a Reverse Member Expansion in OneStream?

options.A: RTreeDescendants
options.B: TreeDescendantsReverse
options.C: ReverseTreeDescendants
options.D: TreeDescendantsR

explanation: D is correct: a Reverse Member Expansion is created by appending R to the end of the expansion name — TreeDescendantsR reverses the display order of members. A is incorrect — the R goes at the end, not the beginning. B is incorrect — TreeDescendantsReverse is not valid OneStream syntax. C is incorrect — ReverseTreeDescendants is not valid OneStream syntax.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: What is the purpose of a Remove Expansion in a OneStream Member Filter?

options.A: To reverse the direction of the order of the results.
options.B: To replace some of the members in the results with alternate members.
options.C: To remove some of the members from the results.
options.D: To permanently delete members from the dimension.

explanation: C is correct: the Remove Expansion removes specific members from the result set generated by a Member Filter — for example, .Remove(None) removes the 'None' member from results. A is incorrect — reversing order is the function of a Reverse Expansion (R suffix). B is incorrect — replacing members is substitution, not Remove. D is incorrect — Remove Expansion affects the display only; it does not delete members from the dimension.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: What would a time function look like if a user wanted to pull in the period one prior to what the workflow is currently set to?

options.A: T#WF
options.B: T#POVPrior1
options.C: T#WFPrior1
options.D: Prior#WF

explanation: C is correct: T#WFPrior1 is the correct syntax — T# is the Time dimension prefix, WF references the workflow period, and Prior1 offsets one period prior. A is incorrect — T#WF is the current workflow period without any offset. B is incorrect — T#POVPrior1 references a period prior to the POV, not the workflow. D is incorrect — Prior#WF is not valid OneStream time function syntax.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: In which two locations are substitution variables available for selection when building a Cube View? (Select 2.)

options.A: The Object Lookup
options.B: The Member Filter Builder Variables tab
options.C: The Member Filter Builder Samples tab
options.D: Cube View General Settings

explanation: A and B are correct: substitution variables can be selected from the Object Lookup and from the Member Filter Builder Variables tab. C is incorrect — the Samples tab shows example filter expressions, not substitution variables. D is incorrect — General Settings manages overall Cube View configuration, not substitution variable selection.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: Which of the following shows the correct syntax for a substitution variable in a OneStream Member Filter?

options.A: T#CVTime
options.B: T#!CVTime!
options.C: |T#CVTime|
options.D: T#|CVTime|

explanation: D is correct: T#|CVTime| is the correct syntax — pipes surround the variable name within the dimension token prefix. A is incorrect — T#CVTime is standard member filter syntax without pipes; not a substitution variable. B is incorrect — exclamation marks delimit parameter names, not substitution variables. C is incorrect — pipes at the very start before the dimension token is incorrect syntax.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: What is the purpose of a Where Clause in a OneStream Member Filter?

options.A: To perform math or business rule operations on specific cells.
options.B: To perform calculations based on data populated in a column or row.
options.C: To allow for further qualification of the results within a Member Filter.
options.D: To retrieve a specific data cell value from the cube.

explanation: C is correct: the Where Clause allows further qualification of Member Filter results by applying conditional logic based on member property criteria — for example, Where(Formula <> '') returns only members with a formula. A is incorrect — math or business rule operations on cells are performed by GetDataCell, not Where Clauses. B is incorrect — column or row calculations use Column/Row expressions. D is incorrect — retrieving specific cell values is the function of GetDataCell.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: Where would a user add a Member Expansion in a Member Filter Builder expression?

options.A: At the beginning of the Member Filter Builder expression.
options.B: In the middle of the Member Filter Builder expression.
options.C: At the end of the Member Filter Builder expression.
options.D: As a standalone separate line in the Member Filter.

explanation: C is correct: Member Expansions are added at the end of the Member Filter expression, appended after the member reference using a period — for example, E#LE_110.TreeDescendants. A is incorrect — beginning placement is not valid syntax. B is incorrect — expansions are not placed in the middle. D is incorrect — expansions are appended directly to the member filter expression, not on separate lines.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: What is the purpose of a Remove Expansion in a OneStream Member Filter?

options.A: To reverse the direction of the order of the results.
options.B: To exclude specific members from the results.
options.C: To replace some of the members in the results.
options.D: To strikethrough members from the filter without removing them.

explanation: B is correct: the Remove Expansion excludes specific members from the Member Filter results. A is incorrect — reversing order is the function of Reverse Expansions (R suffix). C is incorrect — replacing members is substitution, not Remove. D is incorrect — strikethrough is a formatting option, not what Remove Expansion does.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: Which option is an example of a Member Expansion in a Cube View Member Filter?

options.A: E#LE_110.Base
options.D: LE_110.Base

explanation: A is correct: E#LE_110.Base is a Member Expansion — the keyword 'Base' is appended after the member reference using a period. B is incorrect — E#LE_110 is a single member reference without expansion. C is incorrect — a comma-separated list is not a Member Expansion. D is incorrect — missing the dimension token E# required for an Entity member filter.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: What does a GetDataCell calculation do in a OneStream Cube View?

options.A: Allows for further qualification of the results within a Member Filter.
options.B: Retrieves specific cell(s) and performs math or business rule operations.
options.C: Performs calculations based on the data populated in a column or row.
options.D: Identifies which cells in the Cube View contain syntax errors.

explanation: B is correct: GetDataCell retrieves specific data cell(s) from the cube and can perform math or business rule operations on those values — commonly used for ratios, variances, and custom KPIs. A is incorrect — further qualification within a Member Filter is the function of the Where Clause. C is incorrect — column or row data calculations are Column/Row expressions. D is incorrect — GetDataCell does not identify syntax errors.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: What happens when an 'R' is appended to the end of a Member Filter expansion property in OneStream?

options.A: Only members whose names begin with R will be displayed.
options.B: All members in the hierarchy will be renamed with an R prefix.
options.C: The first member displayed will begin with the letter R.
options.D: The order of the members within the hierarchy is reversed.

explanation: D is correct: appending R to a Member Expansion (e.g., TreeDescendantsR) reverses the display order of the members. A is incorrect — the R suffix affects display order, not a filter for member names. B is incorrect — members are not renamed; only their order changes. C is incorrect — the R suffix reverses all members, not just the first.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: What is an example of a Reverse Member Expansion in OneStream?

options.A: TreeDescendantsR
options.B: RTreeDescendants
options.C: TreeDescendantsReverse
options.D: ReverseTreeDescendants

explanation: A is correct: TreeDescendantsR is the correct format — the R is appended at the end of the standard expansion name. B is incorrect — the R goes at the end, not the beginning. C is incorrect — TreeDescendantsReverse is not valid OneStream syntax. D is incorrect — ReverseTreeDescendants is not valid OneStream syntax.

subtopic: Building Cube Views — Member Filter Builder
question: What is the purpose of the Where Clause in a OneStream Member Filter?

options.A: To allow for further qualification of the results within a Member Filter.
options.B: To perform math or business rule operations on specific cells.
options.C: To perform calculations based on the data populated in a column or row.
options.D: To retrieve specific cell values from the cube.

explanation: A is correct: the Where Clause provides further qualification of Member Filter results by applying conditional criteria based on member properties. B is incorrect — math or business rule operations use GetDataCell. C is incorrect — column or row calculations are Column/Row expressions. D is incorrect — cell value retrieval is GetDataCell.

question: Which two approaches can be taken to minimize the effects of database sparsity in OneStream? (Select 2.)

options.A: Utilize suppression settings in Cube Views.
options.B: Delete sparse data intersections from the database.
options.C: Utilize the Extensibility functionality.
options.D: Recycle the database servers on a regular basis.

explanation: A and C are correct: suppression settings prevent sparse intersections from being displayed in Cube Views, improving performance; and Extensibility functionality helps minimize sparsity by targeting relevant data intersections. B is incorrect — manually deleting sparse intersections is not recommended and risks data integrity. D is incorrect — server recycling is a system administration task unrelated to managing sparsity.

question: What is the main purpose of the Paging feature in OneStream Cube Views?

options.A: To organize each dimension into separate pages for easier navigation.
options.B: To enhance the performance of Cube Views containing more than 1,000 unsuppressed rows.
options.C: To enhance the performance of Cube Views containing more than 10,000 unsuppressed rows.
options.D: To organize each dimension member alphabetically by account type.

explanation: B is correct: Paging enhances the performance of large Cube Views by breaking results into pages for Cube Views with more than 1,000 unsuppressed rows. A is incorrect — Paging is a performance feature, not a dimensional organization tool. C is incorrect — the threshold is 1,000 rows, not 10,000. D is incorrect — Paging does not sort members alphabetically.

question: What indicates that a suppressed member could be added to a Cube View?

options.A: An orange slice is displayed in the bottom right-hand corner of the header cells.
options.B: A red slice is displayed in the top right-hand corner of the relevant cell intersection.
options.C: An orange slice is displayed in the top right-hand corner of the relevant cell intersection.
options.D: A red slice is displayed in the bottom right-hand corner of the header cells.

explanation: C is correct: an orange slice in the top right-hand corner of a cell intersection indicates a suppressed member is available to be inserted at that location. A is incorrect — the indicator is at the top right of the cell, not the bottom right of header cells. B is incorrect — the indicator is orange, not red. D is incorrect — it is orange and at the cell intersection, not at header cells.

question: What is the purpose of row and column suppression in OneStream Cube Views?

options.A: To make larger reports easier to read by hiding rows/columns with no meaningful data.
options.B: To hide columns with zero data on smaller reports only.
options.C: To ensure accuracy on smaller reports.
options.D: To hide columns with delayed data on larger reports.

explanation: A is correct: suppression hides rows or columns containing no data, zero values, or invalid intersections, making larger reports easier to read. B is incorrect — suppression applies to any size report, not only smaller ones. C is incorrect — suppression improves readability, not accuracy. D is incorrect — suppression is based on data content, not data latency.

question: Why would a user utilize the Paging feature in a OneStream Cube View?

options.A: To enhance the performance of Cube Views containing more than 1,000 unsuppressed rows.
options.B: To organize each dimension into separate pages.
options.C: To enhance the performance of Cube Views containing more than 10,000 unsuppressed rows.
options.D: To organize each dimension member alphabetically by account type.

explanation: A is correct: Paging is used to enhance performance when a Cube View has more than 1,000 unsuppressed rows by breaking the data into manageable pages. B is incorrect — Paging is a performance tool, not a dimensional organization feature. C is incorrect — the threshold is 1,000 rows, not 10,000. D is incorrect — Paging does not sort members.

question: What happens if sparse row suppression is used with dynamic calculations in a OneStream Cube View?

options.A: Dynamic calculations run faster than when used with default suppression.
options.B: Dynamic calculations are suppressed because their data is not stored in the database.
options.C: Only dynamic calculations returning 'No Data' are suppressed.
options.D: Sparse row suppression has no effect when dynamic calculations are present.

explanation: B is correct: sparse row suppression checks the database for stored data; since dynamic calculations compute values on demand and are not stored in the database, the rows containing them appear empty and are suppressed. A is incorrect — sparse suppression causes dynamic calculations to be hidden, not accelerated. C is incorrect — all dynamic calculation rows are affected, not only those returning No Data. D is incorrect — sparse row suppression significantly affects dynamic calculation rows by suppressing them.

question: Which two approaches can be taken to minimize the effects of database sparsity in OneStream? (Select 2.)

options.A: Utilize suppression settings.
options.B: Delete sparse data intersections from the database.
options.C: Utilize the Extensibility functionality.
options.D: Recycle the database servers on a regular basis.

explanation: A and C are correct: suppression settings hide sparse intersections from reports, and Extensibility functionality manages dimensionality to reduce unnecessary sparse intersections. B is incorrect — manually deleting sparse intersections risks data integrity. D is incorrect — server recycling is unrelated to managing report sparsity.

question: What is the initial output type for a Cube View in OneStream?

options.A: Excel
options.B: PDF
options.C: OneNote
options.D: Web (browser)

explanation: D is correct: the default initial output type for a Cube View in OneStream is Web — rendered in the browser. A is incorrect — Excel is an available export format, not the default initial output. B is incorrect — PDF is used for printing and Report Books, not the default initial output. C is incorrect — OneNote is not a standard OneStream Cube View output type.

question: Why would users apply conditional formatting in OneStream Cube Views?

options.A: To visually explore and analyze data by highlighting it based on defined criteria.
options.B: To copy rows and columns from another Cube View.
options.C: To determine which dimensions are needed for the Cube View.
options.D: To apply data values to members that currently have no data.

explanation: A is correct: conditional formatting is applied to visually explore and analyze data — formatting rules highlight cells based on defined criteria, making patterns and exceptions immediately visible. B is incorrect — Column Sharing copies rows/columns, not conditional formatting. C is incorrect — dimension selection is a design decision, not a formatting function. D is incorrect — conditional formatting changes visual appearance; it does not populate data.

question: What do report headers and footers control in a OneStream Cube View?

options.A: The Auto Fit page width setting for the Cube View.
options.B: Whether gridlines are displayed in the Excel output.
options.C: What appears at the top and bottom of the PDF page output.
options.D: The page break behavior when the report is printed.

explanation: C is correct: report headers and footers control what appears at the top and bottom of the PDF page — including logos, report titles, page numbers, and date/time stamps. A is incorrect — Auto Fit page width is a separate column-sizing setting. B is incorrect — gridline display in Excel is a separate formatting setting. D is incorrect — page break behavior is controlled separately.

question: What do the border settings allow users to update within a OneStream Cube View?

options.A: Font, text color, text size, bold, and italic settings.
options.B: Background color and gridline color.
options.C: Visibility of the column and column width.
options.D: Header labels and footer text.

explanation: B is correct: the Border formatting settings allow users to update the background color and gridline color of cells. A is incorrect — font, text color, size, bold, and italic are Text formatting settings. C is incorrect — column visibility and width are Column formatting settings. D is incorrect — header labels and footer text are in the header/footer sections.

question: What happens if a Cube View report exceeds the width of the page in OneStream?

options.A: XF will prompt users to choose how they want the page to break.
options.B: XF will produce an error until users manually determine how the page should break.
options.C: XF will automatically page break on the appropriate column and repeat the row headers on the following page.
options.D: XF will scale the report to fit within the page width automatically.

explanation: C is correct: when a Cube View exceeds page width, XF automatically applies a page break at the appropriate column and repeats row headers on the following page. A is incorrect — XF handles the break automatically without prompting. B is incorrect — XF does not produce an error; it handles overflow automatically. D is incorrect — XF breaks across pages rather than scaling the content down.

question: Why would users apply conditional formatting in OneStream Cube Views?

options.A: To visually explore and analyze data based on defined criteria.
options.B: To copy rows and columns from another Cube View.
options.C: To determine which dimensions are needed for the report.
options.D: To apply data values to members that have no data.

explanation: A is correct: conditional formatting is applied to visually explore and analyze data by highlighting cells based on defined rules. B is incorrect — Column Sharing copies rows/columns. C is incorrect — dimension selection is a design decision. D is incorrect — conditional formatting changes visual appearance only.

question: What is the purpose of conditional formatting in a OneStream Cube View?

options.A: To share rows and columns from another Cube View.
options.B: To format headers or cells based on defined criteria.
options.C: To determine if users want to display gridlines within Excel.
options.D: To set the default suppression rules for the Cube View.

explanation: B is correct: conditional formatting provides the ability to format headers or cells based on defined criteria — for example, coloring cells red below a threshold or bolding cells that meet specific conditions. A is incorrect — Column Sharing shares rows/columns; not conditional formatting. C is incorrect — gridline display is a separate output option. D is incorrect — suppression rules are configured in row/column or General settings.

question: Which calculation option for Cube Views is created in the Dimension Library on specific dimension members?

options.A: GetDataCell Expressions written directly in a Cube View row.
options.B: Dynamic Calculations written on dimension members.
options.C: Column/Row Expressions defined in the Cube View.
options.D: Formula Passes assigned in Cube View properties.

explanation: B is correct: Dynamic Calculations are created in the Dimension Library on specific dimension members. They use the GetDataCell function to return a calculated value when a Cube View references that member. A is incorrect — GetDataCell expressions in Cube View rows are a different placement, not the Dimension Library approach. C is incorrect — Column/Row Expressions are defined within the Cube View structure itself. D is incorrect — Formula Passes are Member Formula properties, not a Cube View calculation option.

question: Which expression from the Member Filter Builder calculates the difference between two scenarios using the Subtraction function within a GetDataCell?

options.A: Variance
options.B: Better or Worse
options.C: Difference
options.D: Sum

explanation: C is correct: the Difference expression uses the Subtraction function within a GetDataCell to calculate the difference between two scenario values. A is incorrect — Variance is not the specific expression name for the subtraction function. B is incorrect — Better or Worse is a conditional expression based on favorable/unfavorable direction, not the subtraction itself. D is incorrect — Sum adds values, not subtracts.

question: What is another name for using the GetDataCell function to reference Cube View column and row names in a calculation?

options.A: Cube View math
options.B: Column/Row math
options.C: Cube Column math
options.D: Dynamic dimension math

explanation: B is correct: using GetDataCell with references to Cube View column and row names is known as Column/Row math — it allows calculations to reference named row/column intersections within the Cube View. A is incorrect — 'Cube View math' is not the established term. C is incorrect — 'Cube Column math' is not the established term. D is incorrect — 'Dynamic dimension math' is not a OneStream term for this technique.

question: Which two dimensions can contain dynamically calculated members in OneStream? (Select 2.)

options.A: Account
options.B: Entity
options.C: Scenario
options.D: User-Defined (UDs)

explanation: A and D are correct: the Account dimension and User-Defined dimensions (UD1–UD8) can contain dynamically calculated members. The Flow dimension can also contain them. B is incorrect — Entity is a Data Unit dimension and cannot contain dynamically calculated members. C is incorrect — the Scenario dimension does not support dynamic calculated members in the same manner.

question: Which expression from the Member Filter Builder is used to calculate the difference between two scenarios using the Subtraction function within a GetDataCell?

options.A: Variance
options.B: Better or Worse
options.C: Difference
options.D: Prior Period

explanation: C is correct: the Difference expression uses the Subtraction function within GetDataCell to calculate the difference between two scenario values. A is incorrect — Variance is not the specific expression name for subtraction. B is incorrect — Better or Worse is a conditional expression for favorable/unfavorable assessment. D is incorrect — Prior Period is a time comparison concept, not a subtraction expression name.

question: Where can Column Overrides be found within a OneStream Cube View?

options.A: Within Cube View column properties.
options.B: Within Cube View row properties.
options.C: Within Cube View row and column Default properties.
options.D: Within the Cube View General Settings.

explanation: B is correct: Column Overrides are configured within the Cube View row properties. Despite being called 'Column Overrides,' they are accessed through the row settings to allow a specific row to override formatting or calculations for specific columns. A is incorrect — Column Overrides are not in column properties. C is incorrect — Default properties provide general defaults, not override configuration. D is incorrect — General Settings manages overall Cube View configuration.

question: How many Column Overrides can be applied within a single row in a OneStream Cube View?
explanation: C is correct: up to 4 Column Overrides can be applied within a single row, allowing that row to override formatting or calculations for up to 4 different columns. A is incorrect — 2 is below the maximum. B is incorrect — 3 is below the maximum. D is incorrect — 5 exceeds the maximum of 4.

question: When dynamic calculations are running in both columns and rows of a Cube View, which one overrides the other?

options.A: Columns override rows.
options.B: Rows override columns.
options.C: Whichever was saved first takes precedence.
options.D: Neither overrides the other; both calculations run simultaneously.

explanation: B is correct: when dynamic calculations exist in both columns and rows, rows override columns at the intersection. A is incorrect — columns do not override rows; it is the reverse. C is incorrect — save order does not determine precedence. D is incorrect — at a given intersection, only one result is displayed; rows override columns.

question: Which step of a Column Override determines the font settings for a Cube View?

options.A: Row Range
options.B: Member Filter
options.C: Cell Format
options.D: List Parameter

explanation: C is correct: the Cell Format step determines the font and formatting settings for the cells within the override — including font family, size, bold, italic, color, and background. A is incorrect — Row Range defines which rows the override applies to. B is incorrect — Member Filter defines which members are included. D is incorrect — List Parameter defines parameter settings, not font settings.

question: What is the correct syntax for defining a parameter name in OneStream?

options.A: |!ParamView!|
options.B: |ParamView|
options.C: ParamView
options.D: !ParamView!

explanation: A is correct: parameter names must be surrounded by pipes and exclamation marks — for example, |!ParamView!|. B is incorrect — pipes without exclamation marks is incomplete syntax. C is incorrect — plain text without delimiters is not recognized as a parameter. D is incorrect — exclamation marks without pipes is incomplete syntax.

question: What is the purpose of parameters in OneStream?

options.A: To create tables for specified variables in the database.
options.B: To allow data to be filtered at runtime.
options.C: To permanently exclude members from a Cube View.
options.D: To permanently exclude members from a Quick View.

explanation: B is correct: parameters allow data to be filtered at runtime — they enable end users to dynamically select filter values when running a report. A is incorrect — parameters do not create database tables. C is incorrect — permanent exclusions use Member Filters in the Cube View configuration. D is incorrect — parameters enable dynamic selection, not permanent exclusion.

question: Where are parameters built in OneStream?

options.A: Workflow Profiles
options.B: Application Reports
options.C: Workspaces Maintenance Units
options.D: Database tables

explanation: C is correct: parameters are built in Workspaces Maintenance Units within the OneStream application, organizing parameters alongside other workspace components. A is incorrect — Workflow Profiles define process steps and data entry configuration. B is incorrect — Application Reports are pre-built reporting solutions. D is incorrect — parameters are application artifacts, not database entries.

question: How are Literal Value parameters typically used in a OneStream Cube View?

options.A: To correct spelling and grammar mistakes in report text.
options.B: To allow a user to select a member from a drop-down list.
options.C: To retrieve a data value from a cube.
options.D: To format Cube View columns, rows, and dashboard components.

explanation: D is correct: Literal Value parameters hard-code a value that is used to control formatting properties for Cube View columns, rows, and dashboard components — such as colors or display settings. A is incorrect — spelling corrections are made directly in text fields. B is incorrect — member selection from a drop-down is the function of Member List or Delimited List parameters. C is incorrect — retrieving cube data values uses GetDataCell or XFGetCell.
